text:
ashwin: Seeing a perf regression on the 2026-03-15 rollout — tail latency for single-request inference jumped ~2.5x. Need a quick nsys smoke capture to confirm whether kernel selection changed or if KV cache behavior is to blame.

maria: +1. Do a short, focused capture (single inference) with NVTX markers around the request so we can align kernels -> code. Keep duration 3-8s to avoid huge qdrep.

ashwin: Plan: 1) warm GPU once, 2) flush KV cache, 3) run single inference with NVTX begin/end. Want the exact CLI you recommend.

maria: Example I usually run for fast triage:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi,begin,cudaProfilerApi,end \
  --output=quick-smoke --force-overwrite --duration=6s \
  --sample-interval=1ms ./build/bin/serving --config tests/prod-ish.yaml \
```
Notes: 
- NVTX markers: wrap only the RPC handler so unrelated background work is excluded.
- --duration small but long enough to include kernel ramp and KV lookups.
- --force-overwrite to avoid manual file juggling in CI.

simon: If you want sampling instead of full tracing for tiny file sizes: use --sample=cpu (or enable sampling for osrt) and drop cuda trace. That often surfaces scheduler delays without >100MB qdrep.

ashwin: Good point. For a sampling run I'd do:
```
nsys profile --trace=osrt,nvtx --sample-interval=5ms --duration=5s -o sample-run --force-overwrite \
  ./build/bin/serving --run-once --batch-size=1 --kv-cache=clear
```
This gives a lightweight timeline to see where the long wall-clock bursts are.

maria: Also:
- Pin to a single process / single GPU to avoid inter-GPU noise (--cpus-for-gpu maybe in our runner).
- Set env RUNNER_INFER_COUNT=1 and disable background heartbeats.
- For KV cache checks, toggle KV eviction off/on between runs and compare kernel names: eviction shows up as small memcpy-ish kernels + extra kernels during first tokens.

ashwin: After I ran the full trace, I see a new kernel "matmul_split_v2" taking most of the time vs previously "matmul_v1". Timeline shows short stall before kernel launch (~800us). Could be a kernel selection fallback and extra kernel compilation/ptx path.

maria: Look at the kernel compilation markers (nvtx ranges we add around JIT paths) and the osrt sampling heatmap. If we see frequent small launches, it might be our new batching heuristic splitting sequences — check batch planner logs at trace level.

perf-bot: automated-note: saved quick-smoke.qdrep to /artifacts/1709501234/quick-smoke.qdrep (12MB) and sample-run.qdrep (3MB) from 1709501246.

ashwin: Follow-up checklist for triage: 
- Compare qdrep kernel timeline between golden and current.
- grep qdrep export for kernel name changes.
- Run sample-mode (smaller) to confirm whether it's launch overhead vs kernel execution.
- Re-run with --duration 12s to capture any rare eviction spikes.

maria: If it's a kernel-selection fallback, repro locally with env DEBUG_FORCE_KERNEL=v2 to reproduce without long traces; that'll confirm selection logic before diving into nvcc/ptx.

simon: Quick hint: for parsing large qdrep into a flame chart I use: `nsys stats -f csv -o quick-smoke` then `jq`/python to aggregate by kernel name. Saves opening UI for quick diffs.

ashwin: Thanks — running the steps now and will drop qdrep + short notes here. :thumbsup:
